headline: A national register breached through lawful access, and a critical Jira file-read flaw
standfirst: Denmark's CPR breach and Atlassian's unauthenticated arbitrary file-access flaw lead a day otherwise dominated by breach disclosures and law-enforcement news. One distinct CVE appears across the whole selection — do not read the story count as a vulnerability tally.
bodyMarkdown:
## Breaches

Denmark's central person register is the lead story for a reason: the 8.8 million people exposed in the CPR breach [[s26]] were not reached through a perimeter hole but through a company's lawful lookup access to the system. Names, addresses and personal IDs were taken. The editor's framing — that authorised access paths are the softest route into national identity systems — is the point worth keeping; the supplied evidence does not describe how the abuse was detected or what access was withdrawn.

South Korean officials believe AI agents were used against at least seven financial institutions, with personal data on at least 68,000 people reportedly exposed and a Chinese cybersecurity tool said to have been involved [[s5]]. Treat both as stated belief and report: no victims, tool or timeframe are named.

At the FBI, a missed patch by a contractor is being blamed for the ShinyHunters theft of personal information belonging to thousands of bureau employees, and the contractor has been removed [[s8]]. The unpatched system is not described. *Analysis:* the notable element is the accountability framing rather than the vulnerability class — the story as supplied supports only that a patch was missed and a contractor relationship ended.

ASOS confirmed a breach after attackers pushed unauthorised "HACKED" notifications through its mobile app and claimed to have stolen customer data from its Snowflake environment [[s3]]. The confirmation covers the breach and the notifications; the theft claim is the attackers' claim as reported.

## Vulnerabilities

Atlassian's CVE-2026-21589 is the day's most actionable item: CVSS 4.0 score 9.3, Critical, unauthenticated arbitrary file access across eight self-hosted Data Center products — Bitbucket, Confluence, Crowd, Jira Software, Jira Service Management, Bamboo, Crucible and Fisheye [[s1]]. Two constraints matter before anyone panics. Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path, and the flaw does not let an attacker enumerate or list directory contents; the supplied description notes that in some configurations sensitive files in the web application root make it highly severe. The vector is network-reachable with no privileges and no user interaction, and the scope metrics are High. Per-product fix versions are listed in the supplied data, part of which is truncated here, so confirm against Atlassian's own guidance rather than a partial list. KEV enrichment returned a confirmed catalog miss — which is not evidence that exploitation has not occurred.

## Industry

The FBI has arrested a developer of Ploutus ATM malware who was on its ten most wanted list, described as an alleged leader of Tren de Aragua's ATM jackpotting activity [[s11]]. Keep the "alleged": the supplied text does not detail charges, extradition or any operational effect on jackpotting crews beyond the arrest itself.

## Research

A new analysis of the Blinder Tunnel campaign documents an Iran-nexus operation using fake Dubai Airports recruitment lures and GitHub-hosted command-and-control against Iraqi critical infrastructure [[s25]]. Attribution is supplied as given; outcomes and additional malware families are not. The lure-plus-hosted-C2 combination is the transferable tradecraft for energy and government defenders.

CERT-UA found more than 100 compromised Ukrainian websites serving fake Cloudflare verification pages that funnel visitors into a ClickFix trap and deliver the Lunex infostealer [[s10]]. The familiar part is the lure; the less-discussed part is that compromised legitimate sites, not just user behaviour, are the delivery mechanism.

selected.title: Atlassian warns of critical file-access flaw in Jira, Confluence
selected.excerpt: Atlassian is warning customers of a critical vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-21589, that can be exploited for arbitrary file-access in multiple self-hosted Data Center products, including Confluence, Jira, and Bitbucket. [...]

nvd.description: This is a vulnerability in Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center. Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye. This Arbitrary File Access vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path; this vulnerability does not allow attackers to enumerate or list directory contents. In some configurations, there may be some sensitive files that make this highly severe. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. The vulnerability must be addressed for affected versions of: -- Bitbucket Data Center, introduced in version >= 4.6.0, fix versions: 9.4.26, 10.2.8, 10.5.1 -- Confluence Data Center, introduced in version >= 5.10.0, fix versions 9.2.26, 10.2.19 -- Crowd Data Center, introduced in version >= 2.11.0, fix versions 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7, 7.2.4 -- Jira Software Data Center, introduced in version >= 7.1.0, fix versions 9.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Jira Service Management Data Center, introduced in version >= 3.1.0, fix versions 5.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Bamboo Data Center >= 7.0.1, fix versions 10.2.24, 12.1.12 -- Crucible, fix versions 4.9.15 -- Fisheye, fix version 4.9.15 -- Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path. The vulnerability does not include the capability to enumerate or list directory contents.

selected.angle: Atlassian's 9.3-rated unauthenticated arbitrary file-access flaw spans eight self-hosted Data Center products including Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket, so any organization running them internally needs to confirm patched versions today.

selected.title: South Korean officials believe AI agents were used to hack several banks

selected.angle: South Korean officials say AI agents were used to breach at least seven financial institutions and expose data on 68,000 people, an early concrete case of agentic tooling in a real intrusion against regulated finance.

selected.title: ClickFix campaign in Ukraine compromises over 100 websites to spread Lunex malware
selected.excerpt: CERT-UA found fake Cloudflare verification pages that led visitors into a now-familiar ClickFix trap. This time the goal was to infect machines with an infostealer.
selected.angle: CERT-UA found over 100 compromised Ukrainian websites hosting fake Cloudflare verification pages that drop the Lunex infostealer, showing the ClickFix lure format is still scaling and evolving in live campaigns.
